findings.title: chevalleySerre's verdicts for hh, he and hf are never tested where they fail: five mutants that make these three relations hold, or skip a side, pass the whole suite
findings.location: packages/engine/src/rep.ts:363 and 368-370 (holds and the hh, he and hf records); packages/engine/test/golden/p5-rep-units.test.ts:279-338 (the hand cases pass H = 0 and read only the Serre records); packages/engine/test/golden/p5-minuscule.test.ts:259-276 (the only failing case, D4 node 2, fails in ef alone)
findings.claim: No test gives chevalleySerre an input on which an hh, he or hf record fails. As a result, its verdict and its left and right sides for 3 of the 6 relation kinds can be faked and npm test stays green.
findings.expected: SPEC 5.2: a RelationCheck carries both sides and holds is their comparison. rep.ts:333 'General: nothing assumes entries in {0, 1} or a particular basis'. The oracle's chevalley_serre_ok compares sp_comm(H_i,H_j) == {}, sp_comm(H_i,E_j) == C_ij E_j and sp_comm(H_i,F_j) == -C_ij F_j for any E, F, H. RT-11 attack 19 requires a negative case for the comparison of both sides, and COMMON 4.3 requires tests that fail when the behaviour is removed.
findings.observed: These five patches each pass the three phase 5 golden files (168 passed, 168): M33-hh-he-hf-hold (holds true for hh, he, hf), M33-hh-skipped (hh left side never computed), M33-hh-holds, M33-he-right-zero (he's right side equal to its left off the diagonal) and M33-hf-right-left. Under the whole npm test, M33-hh-he-hf-hold gives 3331 of 3333 and M33-hh-skipped gives 3332 of 3333. The only failures are 'Test timed out in 5000ms' in tests that also time out in the unmutated run at load 18, and T12.test.ts passes 56/56 under the mutant with --testTimeout=120000. On every matrix minusculeMatrices builds, hh, he and hf hold whatever the node: H is diagonal with the basis numbers, and E_j and F_j move a basis vector by column j of C. So these mutants change nothing T12 shows, which is why the severity is minor. The gap is in the engine contract. For the hand input of the reproducer, the oracle prints chevalley_serre_ok = False with hh:0,1 left [(0,0,1),(1,1,-1)], he:0,0 right [(0,1,2)], hf:0,0 left [(0,0,1),(1,1,-1)] and right [(1,0,-2)].
findings.reproduction: From a clean checkout of 006f50d plus this branch's files, after npm ci: git apply redteam/rt11-p5/mutants/M33-hh-he-hf-hold.patch, then node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --project engine packages/engine/test/golden/p5- gives exit 0 (168 passed). Then node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --project engine test/unit/redteam-RT-11-hh-he-hf.test.ts gives exit 1 (6 of 7 fail), and after git apply -R it gives exit 0 (7 passed). The same holds for M33-hh-skipped, M33-hh-holds, M33-he-right-zero and M33-hf-right-left: the reproducer fails 2, 2, 1 and 2 tests. The oracle values come from python3 redteam/rt11-p5/rt11_hh_he_hf_oracle.py <worktree>. The runner is bash redteam/rt11-p5/run-batch.sh <wt> engine control <patches> -- packages/engine/test/golden/p5-.
findings.specRef: SPEC 5.2 (RelationCheck with both sides); SPEC 5.7 opening ('recomputes the value with the engine'); CONTRACTS 2.2 RelationCheck; RT-11 attack 19; COMMON 4.3
findings.proposedFix: Adopt packages/engine/test/unit/redteam-RT-11-hh-he-hf.test.ts: hand matrices on A2 with H non-diagonal and E, F nonzero, where hh:0,1, hh:1,0, he:0,0, he:1,0, hf:0,0 and hf:1,0 fail with the oracle's two sides.

findings.title: T12's announcement of a picked relation that fails is never heard by a test: a component that always says 'the two sides are equal' passes T12.spec, M8.spec and T12.test
findings.location: site/src/components/tools/t12/model.ts:625-630 (relationSentence, its 'not equal' branch); site/tests/e2e/T12.spec.ts:239 and 249 (the only relation announcements asserted, both on A2 and both equal); site/tests/unit/tools/T12.test.ts (does not import relationSentence)
findings.claim: The live-region sentence after a relation pick is checked only for relations that hold. A mutant that announces every picked relation as equal survives every T12 and M8 test, while the screen shows 'not equal'.
findings.expected: SPEC 4.0 'Keyboard and screen reader': 'a polite live region announces each result'. SPEC 4 T12 relation checker: 'whether they are equal'. RT-11 attacks 15 and 33. COMMON 4.3.
findings.observed: With S1-relation-sentence-equal.patch (built together with S2 and S4, which touch other code paths): T12.spec.ts plus M8.spec.ts gave 70 passed (5.2m), and T12.test.ts gave 56 passed. The reproducer fails on that build: on ?g=D4&k=2 with relation-j set to 2, data-holds is 'false' and relation-verdict reads 'not equal', but the live region says '[E1, F2] = 0: the two sides are equal.' On the clean build the reproducer passes (1 passed), and T12 plus M8 give 70 passed. The wording is a plan sentence, not a template of 7.5, and the verdict hook is tested, hence minor. This is distinct from P5-RT-05-03 (verdicts from the worker never announced) and P5-RT-05-04 (the formula read visually).
findings.reproduction: git apply redteam/rt11-p5/mutants/S1-relation-sentence-equal.patch; npm run build; PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=<browsers> npx playwright test -c redteam/rt11-p5/rt11-playwright.config.ts site/tests/e2e/T12.spec.ts site/tests/e2e/M8.spec.ts gives exit 0. Then the same command with site/tests/e2e/redteam-RT-11-T12-verdict-announce.spec.ts gives exit 1 (1 failed at line 31). After git apply -R and npm run build, the reproducer gives exit 0.
findings.specRef: SPEC 4.0 Keyboard and screen reader; SPEC 4 T12 (relation checker); SPEC 7.7 Components row; CONTRACTS 5.2
findings.proposedFix: Adopt the reproducer, or add to T12.spec an assertion of the live region after picking a failing relation on D4 node 2 (ef:1,2), and a unit test of relationSentence for both verdicts.

notes: Equivalent on the shipped pages, not reported: S2-digest-failing-zero.patch (and S3, holds forced true) changes the relation digest that a configured T12 state ships for its first render. Every configured T12 state on the site is a minuscule node: the 12 figures of M8 and the A2 node 1 default of /tools/rep/.
